69	> \(vii\) banking fees and expenses (including fees payable to Crestline National Bank under the Subscription Facility);
70	>
71	> \(viii\) third-party consulting, advisory, and expert fees;
72	>
73	> \(ix\) regulatory filing fees and compliance costs;
74	>
75	> \(x\) costs of LPAC meetings, including travel and accommodation expenses of LPAC members;
76	>
77	> \(xi\) costs of litigation and other proceedings involving the Fund or its Investments, including indemnification payments;
78	>
79	> \(xii\) costs of winding up and liquidating the Fund; and
80	>
81	> \(xiii\) any other costs and expenses that are not Organizational Expenses or overhead expenses of the General Partner or the Manager.
82	
83	**(b)** Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Manager shall bear fifty percent (50%) of all broken-deal costs in excess of Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000) per abandoned transaction. For the avoidance of doubt, the Fund shall bear one hundred percent (100%) of the first \$2,000,000 of broken-deal costs per abandoned transaction and fifty percent (50%) of any amount in excess thereof; the remaining fifty percent (50%) of any amount in excess of \$2,000,000 per abandoned transaction shall be borne by the Manager.
84	
85	**(c)** The Fund shall not bear any overhead expenses of the General Partner or the Manager, including office rent, utilities, salaries and compensation of employees, and similar operating costs of the General Partner and the Manager.
86	
87	**[ARTICLE V --- DISTRIBUTIONS; ALLOCATION OF PROFITS AND LOSSES]{.underline}**
88	
89	**Section 5.1 --- Distribution Waterfall**
90	
91	**(a)** Subject to the establishment and maintenance of reasonable reserves as determined by the General Partner, all Distributable Proceeds shall be distributed to the Partners in the following order of priority:
92	
93	> **(i) Return of Capital.** First, one hundred percent (100%) to the Limited Partners (and to the General Partner in respect of its Capital Commitment, but not its Carried Interest) pro rata in proportion to their respective Commitment Percentages, until each Partner has received cumulative distributions under this clause (i) equal to the aggregate Capital Contributions made by such Partner to the Fund.
94	>
95	> **(ii) Preferred Return.** Second, one hundred percent (100%) to the Limited Partners (and to the General Partner in respect of its Capital Commitment) pro rata in proportion to their respective Commitment Percentages, until each such Partner has received cumulative distributions under this clause (ii) equal to a preferred return of eight percent (8%) per annum, compounded annually, calculated on such Partner\'s net capital contributions (i.e., Capital Contributions less prior distributions under clause (i) above) from the date of each such Capital Contribution through the date of each distribution (the \"Preferred Return\"). For purposes of calculating the Preferred Return, Capital Contributions shall be deemed to have been made on the date such contributions were actually funded to the Fund, and prior distributions under clause (i) shall be deemed to reduce net capital contributions as of the date of such prior distribution.
96	>
97	> **(iii) GP Catch-Up.** Third, one hundred percent (100%) to the General Partner until the General Partner has received, in the aggregate (including amounts received under this clause (iii) and clause (iv) below), an amount equal to twenty percent (20%) of the sum of (A) all amounts distributed to all Partners under clause (ii) above and (B) all amounts distributed under this clause (iii). The effect of this clause (iii) is that, once fully achieved, the General Partner will have received twenty percent (20%) of the aggregate Net Profits distributed to all Partners in excess of the Return of Capital.
98	>
99	> **(iv) Residual Split.** Thereafter, eighty percent (80%) to the Limited Partners (and the General Partner in respect of its Capital Commitment) pro rata in proportion to their respective Commitment Percentages and twenty percent (20%) to the General Partner (as \"Carried Interest\").
100	
101	**(b)** The distribution waterfall set forth in this Section 5.1 shall be applied on a whole-fund (aggregated) basis, meaning that the General Partner shall not be entitled to Carried Interest distributions until all Partners have received cumulative distributions equal to their aggregate Capital Contributions and the Preferred Return thereon.
102	
103	**(c)** Distributions shall be made in cash unless otherwise determined by the General Partner. In the event the General Partner determines to make a distribution in kind, such in-kind distribution shall require the prior consent of the LPAC and shall be valued at fair market value as determined by the General Partner in good faith in accordance with Section 7.3. For purposes of the distribution waterfall, in-kind distributions shall be treated as if the distributed property had been sold at fair market value and the proceeds distributed in cash.
104	
105	**(d)** The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to make distributions within thirty (30) days following the receipt of Distributable Proceeds, subject to the establishment of reserves and the retention of amounts necessary to fund the Fund\'s expenses and obligations. The General Partner shall make distributions at least semi-annually during the term of the Fund to the extent Distributable Proceeds are available.
106	
107	**(e)** All distributions to Limited Partners shall be applied first against such Limited Partner\'s unfunded Capital Commitment (to the extent any recycling or recall right would otherwise be available) and then as distributions under the waterfall set forth in this Section 5.1.
108	
109	**Section 5.2 --- Carried Interest**
110	
111	**(a)** The Carried Interest payable to the General Partner equals twenty percent (20%) of Net Profits in excess of the Preferred Return, subject to the GP Catch-Up mechanism described in Section 5.1(a)(iii).
112	
113	**(b)** Carried Interest shall be computed on a whole-fund (aggregated) basis and shall not be subject to a deal-by-deal computation.
114	
115	**(c)** The General Partner may designate one or more individuals (including Marcus Ridgeline, the Senior Managing Directors, and other investment professionals associated with the Manager) to receive allocations and distributions of all or a portion of the Carried Interest. Such designations shall be made by the General Partner in its sole discretion and shall not require the approval of any Limited Partner or the LPAC.
116	
117	**(d)** Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Carried Interest shall be subject to the clawback provisions set forth in Section 5.3.
118	
119	**Section 5.3 --- Clawback**
120	
121	**(a)** Upon the final liquidation and winding up of the Fund, if the General Partner has received aggregate Carried Interest distributions in excess of the amount to which the General Partner would be entitled under the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 5.1 (calculated on an aggregated, cumulative basis as of the date of the final liquidating distribution), the General Partner shall return to the Fund, for distribution to the Limited Partners, such excess Carried Interest distributions (the \"Clawback Amount\").
122	
123	**(b)** The Clawback Amount shall be calculated net of taxes actually paid or deemed payable by the General Partner and its members on such Carried Interest distributions, at an assumed combined federal and state tax rate of forty-five percent (45%). For the avoidance of doubt, the maximum Clawback Amount payable by the General Partner shall be equal to the aggregate excess Carried Interest distributions received by the General Partner, reduced by an amount equal to forty-five percent (45%) of such excess Carried Interest distributions, representing the assumed tax liability of the General Partner and its members with respect to such excess distributions.
124	
125	**(c)** Marcus Ridgeline and each member of the General Partner who has received distributions of Carried Interest shall provide a personal guaranty in favor of the Fund and the Limited Partners, guaranteeing such person\'s pro rata share of the maximum Clawback Amount (net of taxes as set forth in clause (b) above), in a form reasonably satisfactory to the LPAC.
126	
127	**(d)** The Clawback Amount shall be calculated and paid within ninety (90) days of the final liquidating distribution.
128	
129	**(e)** To secure the General Partner\'s obligations under this Section 5.3, the General Partner shall establish and maintain an escrow account (the \"Clawback Escrow\") with an independent, nationally recognized financial institution, into which the General Partner shall deposit an amount equal to no less than thirty percent (30%) of cumulative Carried Interest distributions received by the General Partner. Amounts held in the Clawback Escrow shall be invested in short-term, highly liquid United States Treasury obligations or money market funds, and shall be released to the General Partner only upon the earlier of (i) the final liquidation of the Fund and the satisfaction of all Clawback obligations, or (ii) a determination by the General Partner, with the consent of the LPAC, that the remaining Clawback Escrow balance exceeds the maximum potential Clawback Amount.
130	
131	**(f)** The clawback obligation set forth in this Section 5.3 shall survive the termination of this Agreement and the dissolution of the Fund for a period of three (3) years.
132	
133	**Section 5.4 --- Tax Distributions**
134	
135	**(a)** The General Partner may, in its discretion, make tax distributions to the Partners in amounts estimated to be sufficient to cover each Partner\'s federal, state, and local income tax liability arising from allocations of Net Profits and other items of taxable income of the Fund to such Partner.
136	
137	**(b)** Tax distributions shall be calculated based on an assumed combined federal and state tax rate determined by the General Partner, applied to each Partner\'s allocable share of taxable income for the applicable period. The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to make tax distributions within sixty (60) days following the end of each Fiscal Year in which the Fund has net taxable income.
138	
139	**(c)** All tax distributions shall be treated as advances against and shall reduce future distributions to which the receiving Partner would otherwise be entitled under Section 5.1.
140	
141	**Section 5.5 --- Withholding**
142	
143	**(a)** The Fund and the General Partner are authorized to withhold from any distribution or allocation to any Partner any amounts required to be withheld by the Fund or the General Partner under applicable federal, state, local, or foreign tax law.
144	
145	**(b)** Any amount so withheld shall be treated as having been distributed to the Partner on whose behalf such withholding was made, and the Partner\'s Capital Account shall be adjusted accordingly. To the extent that the amount withheld exceeds the distribution otherwise payable to such Partner, the excess shall be treated as a loan from the Fund to such Partner and shall be repaid from future distributions otherwise payable to such Partner.
146	
147	**[ARTICLE VI --- INVESTMENT PERIOD, INVESTMENT LIMITATIONS, AND KEY PERSONS]{.underline}**
148	
149	**Section 6.1 --- Investment Period**
150	
151	**(a)** The Investment Period shall commence on the Initial Close (June 15, 2022) and shall end on the fifth (5th) anniversary thereof (June 14, 2027), unless earlier terminated or suspended pursuant to this Article VI.
152	
153	**(b)** During the Investment Period, the General Partner may draw down Capital Commitments for new Investments and for any other purpose set forth in Section 3.2. After the expiration or termination of the Investment Period, Capital Commitments may be drawn only for (i) follow-on investments in existing Portfolio Companies, in an aggregate amount not to exceed fifteen percent (15%) of aggregate Capital Commitments, (ii) Fund Expenses, (iii) Management Fees, and (iv) satisfaction of existing commitments, obligations, and liabilities of the Fund. For the avoidance of doubt, after the expiration or termination of the Investment Period, the General Partner shall not make any new Investments on behalf of the Fund.
154	
155	**(c)** The Investment Period may be terminated early upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event and the satisfaction of the conditions set forth in Section 6.3(e). The Investment Period may also be terminated early by the affirmative vote or written consent of Limited Partners holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the aggregate Capital Commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s Capital Commitment).
156	
157	**Section 6.2 --- Investment Limitations**
158	
159	The General Partner shall observe the following limitations with respect to the Fund\'s Investments:
160	
161	**(a)** No more than twenty percent (20%) of aggregate Capital Commitments shall be invested in any single Portfolio Company (calculated at the time of initial investment, based on aggregate cost).
162	
163	**(b)** No more than thirty percent (30%) of aggregate Capital Commitments shall be invested in any single industry sector as classified under the GICS.
164	
165	**(c)** The Fund shall not make investments in (i) real estate or real estate-related assets, (ii) natural resources, mining, or extractive industries, (iii) hostile acquisitions (i.e., acquisitions not supported by the target company\'s board of directors), or (iv) any investment that would cause the Fund to be required to register as an investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940.
166	
167	**(d)** The Fund shall invest primarily in companies with enterprise values between One Hundred Million Dollars (\$100,000,000) and Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$750,000,000). Investments in companies with enterprise values outside this range shall require the prior written approval of the LPAC.
168	
169	**(e)** No more than twenty percent (20%) of aggregate Capital Commitments shall be invested in Portfolio Companies organized or primarily operating outside the United States.
170	
171	**(f)** The General Partner may not borrow on behalf of the Fund in excess of fifteen percent (15%) of aggregate Capital Commitments at any time, excluding the Subscription Facility with Crestline National Bank used to bridge Capital Calls, which Subscription Facility shall be subject to the limitations set forth in Section 3.2(d).
172	
173	**(g)** The investment limitations set forth in this Section 6.2 may be waived with the prior approval of the LPAC, as provided in Section 8.2.
174	
175	**Section 6.3 --- Key Person**
176	
177	**(a) Key Person Definition.** The \"Key Persons\" of the Fund are the individuals identified on Schedule B hereto, being Marcus Ridgeline (Founder, Managing Partner, and Chief Investment Officer) and each of Elena Vasquez, Robert Tanaka, and James Whitfield (each, a \"Senior Managing Director\"). The Key Persons are essential to the Fund\'s investment strategy and the Partners have entered into this Agreement in reliance upon the continued involvement of the Key Persons.
178	
179	**(b) Key Person Event.** A \"Key Person Event\" shall occur if Marcus Ridgeline and at least two (2) of the three (3) Senior Managing Directors cease to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the Fund\'s investment activities, whether by reason of death, disability, resignation, termination of employment, retirement, or any other reason. For purposes of this Section 6.3, \"substantially all\" means at least seventy-five percent (75%) of such person\'s professional working time, measured on a quarterly basis. The departure or reduced involvement of any single Key Person (other than Marcus Ridgeline alone together with at least two Senior Managing Directors) shall not constitute a Key Person Event.
180	
181	**(c) Consequences of Key Person Event.** Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event, the General Partner shall promptly (and in any event within fifteen (15) business days) notify all Limited Partners in writing of the occurrence of the Key Person Event, the identity of the Key Person(s) who have ceased to meet the required time commitment, and the circumstances surrounding the Key Person Event. Following such notification, the Investment Period shall be suspended only upon the affirmative vote or written consent of Limited Partners holding at least sixty percent (60%) of the aggregate Capital Commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s Capital Commitment). During any period of suspension, the General Partner shall not make any new Investments, but may continue to (i) fund follow-on investments in existing Portfolio Companies, (ii) pay Fund Expenses and Management Fees, and (iii) satisfy existing obligations of the Fund.
182	
183	**(d) Cure Period.** Following the notification of a Key Person Event, the General Partner shall have a period of one hundred eighty (180) days (the \"Cure Period\") to either (i) cause the relevant Key Person(s) to resume devoting substantially all of their business time to the Fund\'s investment activities, thereby curing the Key Person Event, or (ii) propose one or more replacement Key Persons to the LPAC. Any replacement Key Person(s) proposed by the General Partner must be approved by the affirmative vote of a majority of the LPAC members, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld. Any replacement Key Person shall have comparable experience and qualifications as the departing Key Person.
184	
185	**(e) Termination of Investment Period.** If the Key Person Event is not cured within the 180-day Cure Period (whether by the return of the relevant Key Person(s) or by the approval of replacement Key Person(s) by the LPAC), and the Limited Partners have voted to suspend the Investment Period in accordance with Section 6.3(c), the Investment Period shall be permanently terminated unless Limited Partners holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of aggregate Capital Commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s Capital Commitment) vote to reinstate the Investment Period. Upon permanent termination of the Investment Period, the Fund shall enter a harvest period and the General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to dispose of Portfolio Company interests and distribute Distributable Proceeds to the Partners.
186	
187	**[ARTICLE VII --- REPORTING AND ACCOUNTING]{.underline}**
188	
189	**Section 7.1 --- Financial Reporting**
190	
191	**(a) Quarterly Reports.** The General Partner shall provide unaudited financial statements and a report on Fund activities to each Limited Partner within ninety (90) days after the end of each calendar quarter. Quarterly reports shall include: (i) an unaudited balance sheet of the Fund, (ii) an unaudited income statement of the Fund, (iii) a statement of changes in partners\' capital, (iv) a schedule of Investments showing, for each Portfolio Company, the cost and fair market value of the Fund\'s investment therein, (v) a summary of investment activity during the quarter (including new Investments, follow-on investments, dispositions, and write-downs), (vi) a summary of Capital Calls and distributions made during the quarter, and (vii) such other information as the General Partner deems appropriate or as may be reasonably requested by the LPAC.
192	
193	**(b) Annual Reports.** The General Partner shall provide annual audited financial statements to each Limited Partner within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each Fiscal Year (December 31). Annual financial statements shall be audited by Haverford Accounting Group LLP (or such other nationally recognized independent public accounting firm as may be engaged by the General Partner) in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles as applied in the United States (\"GAAP\"). Annual reports shall include the audited balance sheet, statement of operations, statement of changes in partners\' capital, statement of cash flows, and notes to the financial statements, together with the auditor\'s report thereon.
194	
195	**(c) Tax Information.** The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide each Partner with its Schedule K-1 (IRS Form 1065) and related tax information within ninety (90) days after the end of each Fiscal Year, or as soon as practicable thereafter. The General Partner shall also provide, upon reasonable request, such additional tax-related information as may be necessary for a Partner to prepare its own tax returns.
196	
197	**(d) Capital Account Statements.** Each Limited Partner shall receive a semi-annual statement of its Capital Account, showing all Capital Contributions, allocations of Net Profits and Net Losses, and distributions during the applicable period.
198	
199	**Section 7.2 --- Fiscal Year**
200	
201	The fiscal year of the Fund shall be the calendar year, commencing on January 1 and ending on December 31 of each year; provided that the first Fiscal Year of the Fund shall begin on the date of the Initial Close and the last Fiscal Year of the Fund shall end on the date of final dissolution.
202	
203	**Section 7.3 --- Valuation**
204	
205	**(a)** Investments shall be valued at fair market value as determined by the General Partner in good faith, in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification 820 (*Fair Value Measurement*) and the IPEV Valuation Guidelines, as each may be updated from time to time.
206	
207	**(b)** The General Partner shall establish and apply a consistent valuation methodology for all Investments, which methodology shall be disclosed to the Limited Partners and the LPAC. The General Partner shall document the basis for each valuation determination, including the valuation methodology applied, the inputs used, and any adjustments made.
208	
209	**(c)** Annual valuations of all Investments shall be reviewed by Haverford Accounting Group LLP in connection with the annual audit of the Fund\'s financial statements.
210	
211	**(d)** The LPAC shall have the right to engage, at Fund expense, an independent third-party valuation firm to review or contest the valuation of any Investment if the LPAC, by majority vote, determines that the General Partner\'s valuation of such Investment is materially inconsistent with the applicable valuation methodology or market conditions. The results of any such third-party valuation review shall be advisory and non-binding unless the General Partner agrees otherwise.
212	
213	**Section 7.4 --- Books and Records**
214	
215	The General Partner shall maintain complete and accurate books and records of the Fund, including all financial records, partnership tax returns, schedules, partnership agreements, Side Letters, Capital Call notices, distribution notices, LPAC meeting minutes, and correspondence with governmental authorities. Such books and records shall be maintained at the Fund\'s principal office at 400 Hamilton Avenue, Suite 3100, Palo Alto, California 94301 (or at such other address as the General Partner may designate). Each Limited Partner shall have the right to inspect and copy the books and records of the Fund during normal business hours upon at least ten (10) business days\' prior written notice to the General Partner, subject to the confidentiality provisions of Article X.
216	
217	**[ARTICLE VIII --- LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE]{.underline}**
218	
219	**Section 8.1 --- Formation and Composition**
220	
221	**(a)** The General Partner shall establish a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"LPAC\") consisting of five (5) members. LPAC members shall be appointed by the General Partner, in the General Partner\'s sole discretion, from among Limited Partners with Capital Commitments of at least One Hundred Million Dollars (\$100,000,000). The General Partner shall select LPAC members based on such factors as the General Partner deems relevant, including the size of the applicable Limited Partner\'s Capital Commitment, the Limited Partner\'s experience and expertise, the need for diversity of perspective, and the absence of conflicts of interest. The General Partner shall endeavor to appoint LPAC members that are broadly representative of the Limited Partner base.
222	
223	**(b)** LPAC members shall serve for the term of the Fund unless they resign, are removed by the General Partner, or their Capital Commitment is reduced below \$100,000,000. The General Partner may remove and replace LPAC members at any time in its sole discretion, provided that any replacement LPAC member meets the \$100,000,000 minimum Capital Commitment threshold.
224	
225	**(c)** No Limited Partner shall have the right to demand appointment to the LPAC, and the General Partner\'s determination with respect to the composition of the LPAC shall be final and binding on all Partners. This Agreement does not provide for any automatic appointment, guaranteed seat, or other mandatory LPAC membership right for any Limited Partner.
226	
227	**(d)** LPAC members shall serve without compensation but shall be reimbursed for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with LPAC activities, including travel and accommodation expenses for attending LPAC meetings.
228	
229	**(e)** The LPAC shall not participate in the control or management of the Fund\'s business and shall serve solely in an advisory, consent, and oversight capacity as set forth in Section 8.2. No LPAC member shall owe any duty to any other Limited Partner solely by virtue of its membership on the LPAC.
230	
231	**Section 8.2 --- LPAC Authority**
232	
233	**(a)** The LPAC shall have authority to review and provide consent or approval with respect to the following matters:
234	
235	> \(i\) Conflict-of-interest transactions between the Fund and the General Partner, the Manager, or any of their respective Affiliates, including any co-investment, allocation, fee-sharing, or other arrangement between the Fund and any other fund or vehicle managed by the Manager or its Affiliates;
236	>
237	> \(ii\) Valuation disputes, including the engagement of an independent third-party valuation firm pursuant to Section 7.3(d);
238	>
239	> \(iii\) Extension of the Fund term pursuant to Section 11.1;
240	>
241	> \(iv\) Waiver of any investment limitation set forth in Section 6.2;
242	>
243	> \(v\) Approval of replacement Key Persons under Section 6.3(d);
244	>
245	> \(vi\) In-kind distributions pursuant to Section 5.1(c);
246	>
247	> \(vii\) Release of amounts from the Clawback Escrow pursuant to Section 5.3(e);
248	>
249	> \(viii\) Any other matter specifically requiring LPAC approval or consent under this Agreement.
250	
251	**(b)** LPAC actions shall require the affirmative vote or written consent of a majority of the LPAC members present at a duly convened meeting (or acting by written consent in lieu of a meeting), provided that a quorum of at least three (3) LPAC members is present or participating. Each LPAC member shall have one vote, regardless of the size of such member\'s Capital Commitment.
252	
253	**(c)** The General Partner shall convene LPAC meetings at least semi-annually. In addition, the General Partner shall convene a meeting of the LPAC within thirty (30) days of any request by a majority of the LPAC members. Meetings may be held in person, by telephone, or by videoconference. The General Partner shall provide LPAC members with reasonable advance notice (not less than ten (10) business days) of each meeting, together with an agenda and any relevant materials.
254	
255	**[ARTICLE IX --- TRANSFERS AND EXCUSE RIGHTS]{.underline}**
256	
257	**Section 9.1 --- Transfer Restrictions**
258	
259	**(a)** No Limited Partner may sell, assign, transfer, pledge, hypothecate, encumber, or otherwise dispose of (each, a \"Transfer\") all or any portion of its Interest in the Fund without the prior written consent of the General Partner, which consent may be withheld in the General Partner\'s sole and absolute discretion. The General Partner shall not be required to provide any reason for withholding its consent to a Transfer.
260	
261	**(b)** Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, no Transfer shall be permitted to:
262	
263	> \(i\) any Person who is not a \"qualified purchaser\" as defined in Section 2(a)(51) of the Investment Company Act of 1940;
264	>
265	> \(ii\) any Person who is not an \"accredited investor\" as defined in Rule 501(a) of Regulation D under the Securities Act;
266	>
267	> \(iii\) any Competitor;
268	>
269	> \(iv\) any Person whose admission as a Limited Partner would cause adverse tax, regulatory, or legal consequences to the Fund or any existing Partner, as determined by the General Partner in good faith; or
270	>
271	> \(v\) any Person if such Transfer would cause the Fund to have a number of Partners that would require the Fund to register under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 or would violate any applicable securities laws.
272	
273	**(c)** Any proposed transferee of an Interest (other than a permitted Affiliate transfer under clause (f) below) must execute a written instrument, in form and substance satisfactory to the General Partner, assuming all of the obligations of the transferring Limited Partner under this Agreement (including unfunded Capital Commitments) and agreeing to be bound by the terms hereof as a substitute Limited Partner.
274	
275	**(d)** Any Transfer made in violation of this Section 9.1 shall be void and of no force or effect, and the Fund and the General Partner shall not be required to recognize any such purported Transfer or the purported transferee as a Partner or to make any distributions or allocations to such purported transferee.
276	
277	**(e)** The transferring Limited Partner shall bear all reasonable costs and expenses incurred by the Fund, the General Partner, and the Manager in connection with any Transfer, including legal fees, accounting fees, and administrative costs, regardless of whether the Transfer is consummated.
278	
279	**(f)** Notwithstanding Section 9.1(a), a Limited Partner may Transfer all or a portion of its Interest to an Affiliate of such Limited Partner without the prior written consent of the General Partner, provided that (i) the transferring Limited Partner provides the General Partner with not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of such Transfer, (ii) the Affiliate transferee meets the requirements of clauses (b)(i) and (b)(ii) above (i.e., is a qualified purchaser and an accredited investor), (iii) the Affiliate transferee is not a Competitor, (iv) the transferring Limited Partner executes and delivers to the General Partner a written acknowledgement that it shall remain jointly and severally liable with the Affiliate transferee for all obligations of the transferee arising under this Agreement (including unfunded Capital Commitments), and (v) the Affiliate transferee executes a counterpart signature page to this Agreement.
280	
281	**Section 9.2 --- Excuse Rights**
282	
283	**(a)** A Limited Partner may request to be excused from participating in a specific Investment only if such participation would violate an applicable legal or regulatory prohibition that is binding on such Limited Partner or would cause such Limited Partner to suffer material adverse legal or regulatory consequences. For purposes of this Section 9.2, \"legal or regulatory prohibition\" means a statute, regulation, order, decree, or binding regulatory directive applicable to the relevant Limited Partner that prohibits such Limited Partner from making or holding the proposed Investment. Investment guidelines, internal policies, board directives, and other non-binding preferences or policies shall not constitute a \"legal or regulatory prohibition\" for purposes of this Section 9.2.
284	
285	**(b)** A Limited Partner seeking to be excused from a particular Investment must deliver written notice to the General Partner, setting forth in reasonable detail the specific legal or regulatory basis for the excuse request, including a citation to the applicable statute, regulation, or regulatory directive, and a description of how such provision prohibits the proposed Investment. Such notice must be delivered to the General Partner prior to the funding of the relevant Capital Call and, in any event, within ten (10) business days of the receipt of the Capital Call notice.
286	
287	**(c)** The General Partner shall determine, in its good faith judgment, whether the asserted legal or regulatory prohibition applies to the requesting Limited Partner with respect to the proposed Investment. In making such determination, the General Partner may request additional information from the requesting Limited Partner, including legal opinions, regulatory filings, or other supporting documentation. **[ARTICLE X --- CONFIDENTIALITY AND MOST FAVORED NATION]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Confidentiality**

**(a)** Each Limited Partner acknowledges and agrees that, in connection with its participation in the Fund, it has received and will receive information of a confidential and proprietary nature. **(b)** Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Limited Partner may disclose Confidential Information:

>
> \(ii\) to any governmental or regulatory authority having jurisdiction over such Limited Partner, to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or regulatory examination (provided that the disclosing Limited Partner shall, to the extent practicable and legally permissible, provide prior written notice to the General Partner of such disclosure and cooperate with the General Partner in seeking confidential treatment of such information);
>
> \(iii\) to the extent required by a valid court order, subpoena, or other compulsory legal process (provided that the disclosing Limited Partner shall, to the extent practicable and legally permissible, provide prompt prior written notice to the General Partner and cooperate with the General Partner in seeking a protective order or other appropriate remedy);

> \(iv\) with the prior written consent of the General Partner, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

**(c)** The General Partner may designate specific information as \"Confidential\" and may restrict the distribution, copying, or reproduction of confidential materials. The General Partner may establish data room protocols and other security measures for the protection of Confidential Information.

**(d)** The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Section 10.1 shall survive the termination of this Agreement and the dissolution of the Fund for a period of three (3) years.

**(e)** The Partners agree that any breach of this Section 10.1 may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages may be an inadequate remedy, and accordingly, any non-breaching party shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief, specific performance, and any other available remedies at law or in equity, without the necessity of posting a bond or other security.

**Section 10.2 --- Most Favored Nation**

**(a)** The General Partner may enter into Side Letters with one or more Limited Partners, granting such Limited Partners rights, benefits, or terms that are different from or in addition to those set forth in this Agreement.

**(b)** Within thirty (30) days following the Final Close (i.e., by October 30, 2022), the General Partner shall provide written notice (the \"MFN Notice\") to each Limited Partner with a Capital Commitment equal to or in excess of One Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$150,000,000) (each, an \"MFN Eligible LP\"), identifying the material economic and reporting terms contained in Side Letters entered into with other Limited Partners. The MFN Notice shall describe the applicable Side Letter provisions in sufficient detail to enable each MFN Eligible LP to evaluate whether it wishes to elect any such term, but shall not be required to disclose the identity of the Limited Partner that is party to any particular Side Letter.

**(c)** Each MFN Eligible LP shall have a period of sixty (60) days following receipt of the MFN Notice (the \"MFN Election Period\") within which to elect, by written notice to the General Partner, to receive the benefit of any identified Side Letter term. Any election made during the MFN Election Period shall be effective as of the date of the applicable Side Letter or the date of the MFN Eligible LP\'s election, whichever is later, and shall apply on a prospective basis unless otherwise agreed by the General Partner.

**(d)** Notwithstanding the foregoing, the MFN election right shall not extend to:

> \(i\) terms granted to accommodate specific regulatory requirements, statutory mandates, or fiduciary obligations applicable to a particular Limited Partner, including governmental entities, public pension systems, and sovereign wealth funds;
>
> \(ii\) terms granted to the General Partner or its Affiliates in their capacity as Partners;
>
> \(iii\) co-investment rights or co-investment allocation provisions; or
>
> \(iv\) LPAC membership or observer rights.

**(e)** The General Partner shall use reasonable efforts to identify all material Side Letter terms in the MFN Notice, but shall not be liable for inadvertent or good faith omissions, provided that any material omitted term shall be made available in a supplemental MFN Notice delivered as promptly as practicable following the discovery of such omission, and the MFN Eligible LPs shall have thirty (30) days following receipt of any supplemental MFN Notice to make additional elections.

**[ARTICLE XI --- TERM AND TERMINATION]{.underline}**

**Section 11.1 --- Fund Term**

**(a)** The Fund shall continue in existence for a period of ten (10) years from the Initial Close (i.e., from June 15, 2022 through June 14, 2032), unless earlier terminated pursuant to Section 11.2 (the \"Fund Term\").

**(b)** The General Partner may extend the Fund Term for up to two (2) additional one-year periods (i.e., the first extension through June 14, 2033, and the second extension through June 14, 2034), in each case with the prior approval of a majority of the LPAC members. The General Partner shall provide the LPAC with at least ninety (90) days\' prior written notice of any proposed extension, together with a written report describing the reasons for the extension, the status of remaining Investments, and the expected timeline for liquidation and distribution.

**(c)** During any extension period, the General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to liquidate and distribute the remaining assets of the Fund in an orderly manner, consistent with the maximization of value for the Partners.

**Section 11.2 --- Early Termination**

**(a)** The Fund may be terminated prior to the expiration of the Fund Term upon the occurrence of any of the following events:

> \(i\) The affirmative vote or written consent of Limited Partners holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the aggregate Capital Commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s Capital Commitment) to dissolve and terminate the Fund;
>
> \(ii\) The entry of a decree of judicial dissolution of the Fund under the Delaware LP Act;
>
> \(iii\) The occurrence of any event that makes it unlawful for the Fund to continue in existence;
>
> \(iv\) The bankruptcy, insolvency, dissolution, or liquidation of the General Partner, or the removal of the General Partner by the Limited Partners in accordance with applicable law, unless a successor General Partner is admitted to the Fund in accordance with this Agreement within ninety (90) days after the occurrence of such event.

**(b)** No Limited Partner shall have the right to withdraw from, or unilaterally terminate its participation in, the Fund except as set forth in this Section 11.2 and Section 9.1 (transfers). Each Limited Partner acknowledges and agrees that its Capital Commitment is irrevocable as set forth in Section 3.1 and that the Fund is intended to be a closed-end investment vehicle with no right of redemption or withdrawal.

**Section 11.3 --- Winding Up and Liquidation**

**(a)** Upon the dissolution of the Fund pursuant to Section 11.1 or Section 11.2, the General Partner (or, if the General Partner is unable to serve, a liquidating trustee appointed by the Limited Partners holding a majority of aggregate Capital Commitments) shall act as the liquidator of the Fund (the \"Liquidator\") and shall proceed to wind up the affairs and liquidate the assets of the Fund.

**(b)** The Liquidator shall dispose of the Fund\'s assets in an orderly manner designed to maximize the value of such assets, shall pay or make reasonable provision for the payment of all debts, liabilities, and obligations of the Fund (including contingent and unliquidated liabilities), and shall distribute the remaining assets of the Fund to the Partners in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 5.1.

**(c)** Distributions upon liquidation shall be made in cash to the extent practicable. In-kind distributions of remaining assets may be made with the prior consent of the LPAC, valued at fair market value as determined by the Liquidator.

**(d)** The Liquidator shall use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the winding up and liquidation of the Fund within twenty-four (24) months following the dissolution event, subject to market conditions and the orderly disposition of illiquid assets.

**(e)** Upon the completion of the winding up and distribution of all Fund assets, the Liquidator shall file a Certificate of Cancellation with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware in accordance with the Delaware LP Act, and the Fund shall thereupon cease to exist as a legal entity.

**(f)** Each Partner shall be furnished with a final statement of the Fund\'s affairs, a final accounting of each Partner\'s Capital Account, and a final Schedule K-1 within ninety (90) days of the final distribution.

**[ARTICLE XII --- INDEMNIFICATION AND EXCULPATION]{.underline}**

**Section 12.1 --- Indemnification**

**(a)** The Fund shall indemnify and hold harmless the General Partner, the Manager, and each of their respective Affiliates, members, partners, directors, officers, employees, agents, and representatives, and each member of the LPAC (each, an \"Indemnified Person\"), from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses, court costs, arbitration fees, and amounts paid in settlement) (collectively, \"Losses\") arising out of or in connection with (i) the Fund\'s activities or operations, (ii) the performance of any Indemnified Person\'s duties or obligations under this Agreement, the Investment Management Agreement, or any other agreement or arrangement related to the Fund, or (iii) any act or omission of an Indemnified Person taken in good faith and in a manner reasonably believed to be in, or not opposed to, the best interests of the Fund.

**(b)** Notwithstanding the foregoing, no Indemnified Person shall be entitled to indemnification under this Section 12.1 for any Losses to the extent arising from or attributable to such Indemnified Person\'s fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence, as determined by a final, non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction.

**(c)** The Fund shall advance expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) to any Indemnified Person in connection with any threatened, pending, or completed action, suit, or proceeding, upon receipt of a written undertaking from such Indemnified Person to repay such advances if it shall ultimately be determined by a final, non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction that such Indemnified Person is not entitled to indemnification under this Section 12.1.

**(d)** The indemnification provided in this Section 12.1 shall be in addition to, and not in limitation of, any other rights to which any Indemnified Person may be entitled under any other agreement, as a matter of law or equity, or under any directors\' and officers\' liability insurance policy maintained by the Fund, and shall inure to the benefit of the successors, assigns, heirs, and legal representatives of each Indemnified Person.

**(e)** The Fund may purchase and maintain directors\' and officers\' liability insurance, errors and omissions insurance, and other insurance coverage on behalf of the Indemnified Persons, at Fund expense, in such amounts and with such coverage as the General Partner deems appropriate.

**Section 12.2 --- Exculpation**

**(a)** No Indemnified Person shall be liable to the Fund or any Partner for any act or omission taken or suffered in good faith and in a manner reasonably believed to be in, or not opposed to, the best interests of the Fund, except for any act or omission constituting fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence, as determined by a final, non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction. The Partners acknowledge that the General Partner, the Manager, and their Affiliates may make errors of judgment in good faith, and such errors shall not give rise to liability absent fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence.

**(b)** The General Partner, the Manager, and their Affiliates may rely, and shall be fully protected in relying, upon the advice and opinions of attorneys, accountants, appraisers, investment bankers, consultants, and other experts and professionals, provided that such reliance is in good faith and the expert or professional is selected with reasonable care.

**(c)** In determining whether any action or omission constitutes gross negligence for purposes of this Section 12.2, the conduct of the relevant Indemnified Person shall be judged against the standard of care applicable to institutional investment managers of similar size, experience, and resources managing funds with similar investment strategies.

**(d)** The exculpation provided in this Section 12.2 shall be uniform with respect to all Limited Partners. The General Partner and the Manager shall owe the same duties and be subject to the same standard of care with respect to all Limited Partners equally, and no Limited Partner shall be entitled to a different or enhanced standard of care from the General Partner or the Manager except as may be separately agreed in a Side Letter (subject to the limitations set forth in this Agreement).

**Section 12.3 --- Limitation on Liability**

**(a)** Except as provided in Section 5.3 (Clawback), the General Partner\'s aggregate liability to the Fund and the Limited Partners shall in no event exceed the General Partner\'s Capital Commitment to the Fund.

**(b)** No Limited Partner shall be liable for the debts, obligations, or liabilities of the Fund in excess of such Limited Partner\'s unfunded Capital Commitment, together with the amount of any distributions received by such Limited Partner that are required to be returned pursuant to this Agreement or the Delaware LP Act.

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, RGBColor, Inches
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

doc = Document()
sec = doc.sections[0]
sec.left_margin = sec.right_margin = Inches(0.9)
sec.top_margin = sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.9)
st = doc.styles["Normal"]; st.font.name = "Calibri"; st.font.size = Pt(10.5)
for lvl, sz in ((1, 13), (2, 11.5), (3, 10.5)):
    h = doc.styles["Heading %d" % lvl]; h.font.name = "Calibri"; h.font.size = Pt(sz); h.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1F,0x3A,0x5F)

def shade(cell, color):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); s = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    s.set(qn("w:val"), "clear"); s.set(qn("w:color"), "auto"); s.set(qn("w:fill"), color); tcPr.append(s)

def P(text="", bold=False, italic=False, style=None, size=None, align=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style) if style else doc.add_paragraph()
    add_runs(p, text, bold, italic, size)
    if align: p.alignment = align
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(5)
    return p

def add_runs(p, text, bold=False, italic=False, size=None):
    # **bold** markup support
    parts = text.split("**")
    for i, part in enumerate(parts):
        if not part: continue
        r = p.add_run(part); r.bold = bold or (i % 2 == 1); r.italic = italic
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)

def B(text, level=0):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet" if level == 0 else "List Bullet 2")
    add_runs(p, text); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3); return p

def N(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Number"); add_runs(p, text); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3); return p

def H(text, lvl=1): return doc.add_heading(text, level=lvl)

def T(headers, rows, widths=None, size=8.5, head_color="1F3A5F"):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers)); t.style = "Table Grid"; t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.text = ""; r = c.paragraphs[0].add_run(h); r.bold = True; r.font.size = Pt(size); r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF,0xFF,0xFF); shade(c, head_color)
    for row in rows:
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i, v in enumerate(row):
            cells[i].text = ""; p = cells[i].paragraphs[0]; add_runs(p, str(v), size=size)
            if str(v).startswith("HIGH"): shade(cells[i], "F4CCCC")
            elif str(v).startswith("MEDIUM"): shade(cells[i], "FCE5CD")

        for row in t.rows:

    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

(dated June 15, 2022, as amended through the Final Close of September 30, 2022), and Verification of the CIO’s Investment Committee Approval Memorandum")]

# ---------------- I. Executive summary ----------------
H("I. Executive Summary")
P("We compared each provision of the PBPEPS Side Letter (the “Side Letter” or “SL”) against the corresponding provisions of the RGEF IV LPA (the “LPA”), and tested each statement in the CIO’s email memorandum requesting Investment Committee approval (the “IC Memo”) against both documents. Our bottom line: **the Side Letter delivers several real economic and reporting improvements, but the IC Memo materially overstates what PBPEPS is getting.** Five of the twelve concessions listed in the IC Memo are either misdescribed or are at serious risk of being unenforceable under the LPA’s own conflict rules. The Investment Committee should not rely on the IC Memo as currently written.")
P("Key findings (in order of significance):", bold=True)
B("**The LPA’s “notwithstanding” rule undermines four headline concessions.** LPA § 13.5(b) provides that a Side Letter controls over a conflicting LPA term **only if the Side Letter contains express “notwithstanding” language specifically overriding identified LPA provisions**; otherwise the LPA governs and the side letter is read as supplemental and “not in derogation of” the LPA. The Clawback Enhancement (SL § 7: “In addition to … Section 5.3”), Key Person automatic suspension (SL § 6: “In addition to … Section 6.3”), Guaranteed LPAC Seat (SL § 5(a): “In addition to … Section 8.1”) and Withdrawal Right (SL § 9: no override language at all) each directly contradict an LPA provision but lack the required override. The SL’s own general conflict clause (“the terms of this Side Letter shall control”) does not satisfy § 13.5(b), which demands provision-specific language. The IC Memo’s statement that the SL’s “provisions control in the event of any inconsistency with the LPA” (IC Memo § 5) is therefore incorrect as a matter of the LPA’s terms.")
B("**The IC Memo misstates two hard numbers.** The co-investment threshold is **$125,000,000** in SL § 3(a)–(b), not $100,000,000 as stated in IC Memo Table row 2 and § 4. The withdrawal Deployment Threshold is **50% ($1.39 billion)** in SL § 9, not 40% as stated in IC Memo Table row 11. Both errors make the concessions look more valuable than they are.")
B("**The clawback is described as “notwithstanding the LPA” when it is not**, and its value is overstated. The IC Memo (Table row 10; § 4) says the gross clawback applies “notwithstanding the LPA” — the SL actually says “in addition to.” The IC Memo’s $10 million illustration also implies PBPEPS recovers the full $4.5 million incremental amount; PBPEPS’s economic share of a Fund-level clawback is its ~6.295% Commitment Percentage (≈ $283,000 on those facts). The gross-up is also unsupported by the LPA’s escrow (30% of carry, § 5.3(e)) and personal guaranties (capped at the net-of-tax amount, § 5.3(c)).")
B("**The MFN may be a step backwards, not forward.** SL § 2 (which does override LPA § 10.2) limits PBPEPS’s election to terms granted to LPs whose commitments are **equal to or less than $175 million**. LPA § 10.2 contains no such size limit — an MFN Eligible LP may elect terms from any other LP’s side letter. Read literally, the SL replaces the broader LPA MFN with a narrower one that excludes the largest (and typically best-treated) investors. The IC Memo’s claim that the MFN “ensures PBPEPS receives best available terms” is inaccurate. The SL does improve timing (15-day notice / 90-day election vs. 30/60), retroactivity, and includes co-investment rights (excluded by LPA § 10.2(d)(iii)).")
B("**The Key Person “enhancement” does not change the trigger**, which remains identical to the LPA (Marcus Ridgeline **and** two of three Senior Managing Directors — i.e., three of four Key Persons must depart). Further, a fund-wide suspension of the Investment Period cannot be effected by one LP’s side letter without affecting other LPs (LPA §§ 13.5(c), 14.1(d)), and the SL’s resumption mechanics are in some respects **weaker** than the LPA (resumption on designation of replacements acceptable to PBPEPS alone, bypassing LPAC approval under § 6.3(d), or on a 60% LP vote versus the 75% reinstatement vote in § 6.3(e)).")
B("**The Withdrawal Right conflicts with the LPA’s core closed-end architecture** (§ 3.1(b) irrevocable commitments; § 11.2(b) “no right of redemption or withdrawal” except per §§ 11.2 and 9.1) and would require a cash distribution of NAV out of a pooled vehicle, affecting other LPs. Its enforceability is doubtful; even if enforceable, the Election Period (June 15 – August 14, 2025) has now passed and its status must be confirmed.")
B("**The negligence exculpation standard (SL § 8) is properly overridden but practically limited**: it does not override the LPA § 12.3(a) cap limiting GP liability to its $55.6 million Capital Commitment; SL § 8(b) restricts Fund (not GP) indemnification, which impacts pooled Fund assets and so other LPs (§ 14.1(d)); and the IC Memo omits SL § 8(b) entirely.")
B("**Several drafting errors** require correction: wrong cross-references (SL § 7 to LPA § 5.3(c) for escrow — escrow is § 5.3(e); SL § 9(b) to § 7.2 for valuation — valuation is § 7.3; SL § 11(e) to § 13.4 for notices — notices are § 13.3); a waiver of a non-existent “minimum transfer size requirement” in § 9.1; notices to “addresses set forth in the preamble” where the GP’s address does not appear; outdated CPRA citation (Gov. Code § 6250 et seq. was recodified at § 7920.000 et seq. effective January 1, 2023); and inconsistent fund-counsel name (letterhead “Graystone Kirkland LLP” vs. LPA “Graystone Hargrove LLP”).")
P("Recommendation: The Investment Committee should (i) be provided with a corrected IC Memo; and (ii) PBPEPS should require, before execution (or, if already executed, by way of a confirmatory amendment under SL § 11(a)), an amended Side Letter that adds express provision-specific “notwithstanding” language to SL §§ 5(a), 6, 7 and 9, removes the size limitation from the MFN (or expressly preserves the LPA § 10.2 MFN in addition), corrects the cross-references, and conforms the economic figures. Detailed recommendations appear in Part VIII.", bold=False)

# ---------------- V. Detailed analysis ----------------
H("V. Detailed Analysis of Material Deviations")

H("1. Management Fee (SL § 1; LPA § 4.1)", 2)
P("SL § 1 validly overrides § 4.1 (express “notwithstanding” language, reinforced by § 4.1(g)). The reduction is 25 bps in each period. Our recalculation:")
T(["Period", "LPA Fee", "SL Fee", "Annual Saving", "Period Saving", "Comment"], [
 ["Investment Period (6/15/2022–6/14/2027)", "$3,062,500/yr (1.75% × $175M)", "$2,625,000/yr (1.50% × $175M)", "$437,500", "$2,187,500", "Firm — based on Commitment"],
 ["Post-IP (6/15/2027–6/14/2032)", "1.50% × Invested Capital", "1.25% × Invested Capital", "≤ $437,500", "≤ $2,187,500", "Ceiling only: assumes $175M invested and never reduced by realizations/write-downs; actual likely materially lower"],
 ["Extensions (to 6/14/2034, § 11.1(b))", "1.50% × Invested Capital", "1.25% × Invested Capital", "Variable", "Variable", "Not addressed in IC Memo"],
], widths=[1.4, 1.1, 1.1, 0.8, 0.8, 1.5])
P("Observations: (a) the IC Memo’s “$4,375,000” should be presented as a maximum; a realistic post-IP figure is substantially below $2.19 million because invested capital is reduced by full realizations and write-downs to zero under § 4.1(b); (b) because PBPEPS is MFN-eligible under LPA § 10.2 (and other ≥$150M LPs may elect PBPEPS’s fee term, which is not within any § 10.2(d) carve-out), the GP may later resist granting further concessions; (c) the SL refers to the fee as payable to “the General Partner (or … the Manager)” — § 4.1(c) makes it payable to the Manager; harmless but should be conformed.")

H("2. Most Favored Nation (SL § 2; LPA § 10.2)", 2)
P("SL § 2 is introduced by “Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Section 10.2,” which under § 13.5(b) is effective. That cuts both ways: it means the SL formulation **replaces** § 10.2 for PBPEPS to the extent inconsistent. The key deviations are:")
B("**Narrower universe of source side letters.** SL § 2 extends only to terms granted to LPs “whose Capital Commitment … is equal to or less than” $175 million. LPA § 10.2(b)–(c) has no such limit. PBPEPS (6.295% of commitments) is unlikely to be the largest LP in a $2.78 billion fund; anchor investors with larger commitments typically receive the most favorable terms, and PBPEPS would be excluded from them. This is the single most significant economic drafting point in the SL and is not disclosed in the IC Memo.")
B("**Improvements:** 15-day notice (by October 15, 2022) versus 30 days (October 30, 2022); 90-day versus 60-day election period; redacted copies of side letters rather than a summary; effectiveness from admission (retroactive) versus the LPA’s prospective effect (§ 10.2(c)); a narrower regulatory carve-out (only terms “not applicable to the Investor”) versus § 10.2(d)(i)’s broad carve-out for any public-pension accommodation; and co-investment rights are included (§ 10.2(d)(iii) excludes them). The SL is silent on the LPAC exclusion (§ 10.2(d)(iv)).")
B("**Gaps:** limited to “economic or reporting” terms (governance protections such as key person, transfer, excuse and LPAC rights may fall outside); no express coverage of side letters entered into after the Final Close (e.g., with transferees) or of supplemental MFN Notices under § 10.2(e); no remedy beyond self-executing effectiveness if the GP fails to give notice.")
P("Recommendation: delete the size limitation or, at a minimum, add: “The rights of the Investor under this Section 2 are in addition to, and not in limitation of, the rights of the Investor as an MFN Eligible LP under Section 10.2 of the Partnership Agreement, and the Investor may elect under whichever provision is more favorable.”")

H("3. Co-Investment Rights (SL § 3)", 2)
P("The IC Memo states the threshold twice as $100 million; SL § 3(a), § 3(b) and the closing paragraph of § 3 all state **$125,000,000**. The SL’s worked example (Fund equity $200M; excess $75M; allocation $4,717,500 at 6.29%) is arithmetically correct at the rounded rate (≈$4,721,000 at Schedule A’s 6.2950%). Given the Fund’s $100–$750 million EV focus and the 20% single-company limit (≈$556 million, § 6.2(a)), equity cheques above $125 million will occur only in the larger transactions, so the right will be exercised infrequently. Other points: (a) the definition of the Fund’s “aggregate equity commitment (including any equity commitment made through a co-investment vehicle)” is circular and could inflate or deflate the threshold; (b) the obligation is “subject to [the GP’s] fiduciary obligations” and regulatory constraints — a broad escape; (c) co-investment vehicles organised by the GP are “Affiliates” under the LPA definition, so § 8.2(a)(i) LPAC conflict consent may be required; (d) expenses of the co-investment vehicle and broken-deal cost sharing are unaddressed; (e) the SL right is protected from other LPs’ MFN by § 10.2(d)(iii), which is favorable to PBPEPS’s exclusivity.")

H("4. Transfer Rights (SL § 4; LPA § 9.1)", 2)
P("SL § 4 effectively removes the GP’s § 9.1(a) sole-discretion consent for transfers to US state governmental pension plans, subject to notice, assumption, legal opinion and compliance conditions. Points of deviation and risk:")
B("**Competitor bar.** LPA § 9.1(b) opens with “Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement” and prohibits transfers to any Competitor. The “Competitor” definition (§ 1.1) expressly sweeps in “pension system[s]” that manage or advise a fund with a substantially similar strategy. A GP could argue that a state pension plan with an in-house growth equity or co-investment program is a Competitor, and that SL § 4’s general override of “Section 9.1” does not reach § 9.1(b)(iii). The SL should state expressly that a governmental pension plan shall not be deemed a Competitor solely by reason of its in-house investment activities.")
B("**Eligibility bars retained by implication.** The SL does not expressly preserve or waive the § 9.1(b)(i)–(ii) qualified purchaser / accredited investor requirements; the legal opinion requirement partly covers this. Clarity is recommended.")
B("**Non-existent requirement.** SL § 4 waives “the minimum transfer size requirements set forth in Section 9.1” — § 9.1 contains no minimum transfer size. Either a requirement was dropped from the LPA or the SL was drafted from a different precedent; confirm.")
B("**Costs.** SL waives any “transfer fee or administrative charge”; § 9.1(e) separately requires the transferor to bear the Fund’s legal, accounting and administrative costs. The SL’s waiver is broader in wording only as to “fee or charge” — clarify that § 9.1(e) costs are also waived (or capped).")
B("**IC Memo overstatement.** The IC Memo’s reference to “co-investing sister funds” is not supported; only governmental pension plans organised under US state law qualify. Non-governmental affiliates must use § 9.1(f), which requires PBPEPS to remain jointly and severally liable.")
B("**Positive:** transferees inherit SL rights (§ 4 and § 11(b)), including the negligence standard (SL § 8(a)), and PBPEPS is not made jointly and severally liable post-transfer (contrast § 9.1(f)(iv)).")

H("5. LPAC Seat (SL § 5(a); LPA § 8.1)", 2)
P("LPA § 8.1(c) states that “No Limited Partner shall have the right to demand appointment to the LPAC … This Agreement does not provide for any automatic appointment, guaranteed seat, or other mandatory LPAC membership right for any Limited Partner,” and § 8.1(b) permits the GP to “remove and replace LPAC members at any time in its sole discretion.” SL § 5(a) is expressed to be “In addition to the provisions of Section 8.1” and expressly acknowledges that the LPAC operates “in accordance with Section 8.1.” Under § 13.5(b), absent a “notwithstanding” override, the LPA governs and the SL is “not in derogation of” it. Although the SL calls the seat a “binding obligation” and “material inducement,” the GP has a credible argument that it may remove PBPEPS under § 8.1(b). PBPEPS would at most have a contract claim against the GP (not a right to sit). Additional points: the seat would be lost under § 8.1(b) if PBPEPS’s commitment is reduced below $100 million (e.g., through excuse reductions under SL § 5(b)/LPA § 9.2(d) or partial transfers); and the seat is personal to PBPEPS (it is not MFN-able by others under § 10.2(d)(iv)).")
P("Fix: “Notwithstanding Sections 8.1(a), 8.1(b) and 8.1(c) of the Partnership Agreement, the Investor shall be entitled to appoint one member of the LPAC for the term of the Fund, and the General Partner shall not remove the Investor’s representative without the Investor’s consent, provided the Investor’s Capital Commitment is not less than $100,000,000 (disregarding reductions resulting from excused investments).”")

H("6. Excuse Rights (SL § 5(b); LPA § 9.2)", 2)
P("SL § 5(b) validly overrides § 9.2 (express “notwithstanding”) and is a genuine expansion: § 9.2(a) and (f) expressly prohibit excuse based on “board-adopted investment parameters, social responsibility policies [or] environmental policies,” whereas SL § 5(b)(ii) allows excuse on an objective 15% revenue test irrespective of statutory compulsion. Issues: (a) **Timing** — the 15-business-day notice period runs from receipt of the capital call notice, and § 3.2(a)(iv) permits a funding date only 15 business days after notice; PBPEPS should require advance notice of prospective investments (not merely the call) and confirm that a timely excuse notice suspends the funding obligation; (b) **Determination** — because SL § 5(b) is stated to be “in addition to” § 9.2, the GP could argue the § 9.2(c) GP good-faith determination applies; the SL should make PBPEPS’s determination conclusive for § 5(b)(ii); (c) **Statutory basis** — the IC Memo characterises California Government Code §§ 7500–7914 as imposing “divestment mandates related to tobacco, firearms, and thermal coal.” Several California divestment statutes apply by their terms only to specified systems (e.g., CalPERS/CalSTRS); PBPEPS’s regulatory counsel should confirm which mandates actually bind PBPEPS. To the extent they do not, SL § 5(b)(ii) (the revenue test) remains the operative protection; (d) **Overlap** — LPA § 6.2(c)(ii) already prohibits natural resources, mining or extractive investments, so thermal coal producers are largely excluded at Fund level; (e) the forfeiture language (“share of any distributions attributable to such excused investment shall be forfeited”) is consistent with § 9.2(e) but should be clarified to confirm no penalty on PBPEPS’s other investments and that Management Fees are not charged on the reduced commitment.")

H("7. Key Person (SL § 6; LPA § 6.3)", 2)
P("The IC Memo presents automatic suspension as “materially stronger protection.” Our analysis is that the protection is largely illusory as drafted:")
B("**No override.** SL § 6 is “In addition to” § 6.3. LPA § 6.3(c) states the Investment Period “shall be suspended **only** upon the affirmative vote or written consent of Limited Partners holding at least sixty percent (60%)” — a direct conflict. Under § 13.5(b), the LPA governs.")
B("**Fund-wide effect.** The Investment Period is a single fund-wide period. An automatic suspension for all LPs triggered by one LP’s side letter would “directly or indirectly alter” other LPs’ rights (§ 14.1(d); § 13.5(c)). A PBPEPS-only suspension (i.e., excuse from new-investment capital calls during a KPE) is the enforceable alternative and should be drafted as such.")
B("**Trigger unchanged.** Both documents require that Marcus Ridgeline **and** at least two of three SMDs cease to devote ≥75% of their time (§ 6.3(b)). Three of four Key Persons must depart before anything happens. A market-standard investor ask would be “Marcus Ridgeline **or** any two SMDs.” The final sentence of § 6.3(b) is also internally garbled and should be clarified.")
B("**Weaker resumption.** SL § 6 resumes the Investment Period on the earlier of (a) replacements “reasonably acceptable to the Investor” or (b) a 60% LP vote. LPA § 6.3(d) requires LPAC majority approval of replacements with comparable qualifications, and § 6.3(e) requires a 75% vote to reinstate after an uncured KPE. If SL § 6 were effective, it would allow resumption on a lower threshold than the LPA.")
B("**Follow-on cap.** SL § 6 caps follow-ons during suspension at 15% of Commitments (consistent with § 6.1(b)); LPA § 6.3(c) contains no cap during suspension — a modest improvement.")

H("8. Clawback Enhancement (SL § 7; LPA § 5.3)", 2)
P("LPA § 5.3(b) provides that the Clawback Amount “shall be calculated net of taxes … at an assumed combined federal and state tax rate of forty-five percent (45%)” and that the “maximum Clawback Amount” is the excess reduced by 45%. SL § 7 is “In addition to” § 5.3 and directly contradicts § 5.3(b). Under § 13.5(b), the LPA formula governs. The IC Memo states the enhancement applies “notwithstanding the LPA” (Table row 10; § 4) — that is not what the SL says.")
P("Even if enforceable, the economics are overstated. The clawback is paid “to the Fund, for distribution to the Limited Partners” (§ 5.3(a)), so PBPEPS’s benefit is its pro rata share. On the IC Memo’s own illustration ($10M excess carry): LPA net clawback = $5.5M; gross = $10M; incremental Fund-level recovery = $4.5M; PBPEPS share ≈ 6.295% × $4.5M ≈ **$283,000**, not $4.5M. SL § 7’s phrasing that “the full amount of any excess carried interest distributions … shall be returned to the Investor” is ambiguous and should be clarified to refer to the Investor’s attributable share.")
P("Security mismatch: § 5.3(e) escrow is only 30% of cumulative carry and the § 5.3(c) personal guaranties cover only the net-of-tax amount. SL § 7 refers to the escrow as “Section 5.3(c)” (wrong; it is § 5.3(e)) and requires the GP to “ensure” escrow sufficiency without specifying a top-up mechanism. The SL should expressly override §§ 5.3(b) and 5.3(c), require guaranties of the gross amount, and specify a PBPEPS-specific escrow reserve or top-up.")

H("9. Exculpation and Indemnification (SL § 8; LPA Article XII)", 2)
P("SL § 8 properly overrides §§ 12.1 and 12.2 and is contemplated by § 12.2(d). However: (a) **§ 12.3(a) cap** — GP aggregate liability to the Fund and LPs is capped at the GP’s $55.6M Capital Commitment (clawback excepted) and SL § 8 does not override § 12.3; (b) **scope** — SL § 8(c) defines “investment decisions in which the Investor’s capital is deployed” to cover virtually every Fund investment, which is favorable but heightens the GP’s argument that the provision affects the Fund as a whole; (c) **Fund indemnity** — SL § 8(b) limits the Fund’s duty to indemnify the GP/Manager for negligence; because indemnity is paid from pooled Fund assets, this indirectly benefits all LPs, but if the GP contends it alters the indemnification relationship with other LPs (§ 14.1(d)) enforceability may be contested; (d) **Manager** — the Manager signs only an acknowledgement “solely with respect to Section 8”; the Investment Management Agreement (not reviewed) should be checked for inconsistent exculpation; (e) **forum** — claims proceed by AAA arbitration in Wilmington (§ 13.2), with each side bearing its own costs (§ 13.2(d)); (f) the IC Memo omits the § 8(b) indemnity change altogether.")

H("10. Withdrawal Right (SL § 9; LPA §§ 3.1(b), 11.2(b))", 2)
P("The IC Memo states the Deployment Threshold as 40%; SL § 9 states **50%** ($1,390,000,000 of $2,780,000,000), measured on “funded investments and binding commitments” as of June 15, 2025. LPA § 3.1(b) makes commitments irrevocable “except as expressly provided in this Agreement,” and § 11.2(b) states that no LP may withdraw “except as set forth in this Section 11.2 and Section 9.1” and that the Fund has “no right of redemption or withdrawal.” SL § 9 contains no override language and therefore, under § 13.5(b), is at material risk of being unenforceable. In addition, payment of PBPEPS’s share of NAV in cash within 180 days would require liquidation or borrowing at Fund level, diluting or burdening other LPs (§§ 13.5(c), 14.1(d)) — notwithstanding SL § 9’s statement that other LPs need not increase commitments.")
P("Mechanical issues: (a) the valuation cross-reference to “Section 7.2” is to the Fiscal Year provision — valuation is § 7.3; (b) the sequence of a 60-day Election Period followed by a 90-day Withdrawal Notice and a 180-day valuation/payment window leaves PBPEPS exposed to capital calls during the notice period (SL § 9(d) only preserves calls “issued prior to the date of the Withdrawal Notice,” which is favorable, but the “effective date” of withdrawal is not defined); (c) “binding commitments” counting toward deployment is GP-favorable and undefined; (d) the GP’s reserve right for contingent liabilities is uncapped; (e) **timing** — the Election Period ran from June 15 to August 14, 2025. If the SL was executed, PBPEPS should confirm whether the Deployment Threshold was tested and whether the right lapsed.")

H("11. Reporting and CPRA (SL § 10; LPA §§ 7.1, 10.1)", 2)
P("SL § 10(a) properly overrides § 7.1 and shortens deadlines (60/90 days) and adds monthly portfolio summaries. However, the closing paragraph converts these into “commercially reasonable efforts” obligations with a no-breach carve-out for circumstances beyond the GP’s control; the IC Memo does not mention this. The 90-day audited deadline may be impracticable if the auditor’s timetable is driven by the LPA’s 120-day standard; PBPEPS should confirm with the GP that Haverford Accounting Group has been engaged on that basis.")
P("SL § 10(b) properly overrides § 10.1 as to GP designation practice, but it does not expressly amend PBPEPS’s own confidentiality covenant in § 10.1(a), whose exceptions (§ 10.1(b)) do not mention public records laws. SL § 11(f)(ii) covers disclosure of the SL itself “as may be required by applicable law … including … the CPRA,” but not Fund information generally. Recommended: add an express carve-out permitting PBPEPS to make any disclosure it reasonably determines is required under the CPRA (now Gov. Code § 7920.000 et seq.) or other public records law, including disclosures mandated for alternative investment vehicles. Also: the ≥10-business-day prior notice to the GP “where practicable” can conflict with the CPRA’s 10-day initial response period; the “designated as confidential by such portfolio company” exception lets portfolio companies self-designate; and the statutory citation (§ 6250 et seq.) should be updated.")

H("12. General Provisions (SL § 11)", 2)
B("**No governing law or dispute resolution clause.** The IC Memo’s LPA baseline cites Delaware law (§ 13.1) and AAA arbitration (§ 13.2), but the SL itself is silent. Because the SL “forms a part of” the LPA, LPA §§ 13.1–13.2 likely apply; this should be stated expressly. PBPEPS should also confirm whether, as a California public entity, it requires a California-venue or sovereign-immunity reservation.")
B("**Notices.** SL § 11(e) refers to “Section 13.4” for notice mechanics (§ 13.4 is Successors and Assigns; notices are § 13.3) and to addresses “set forth in the preamble,” which include only PBPEPS’s address.")
B("**Amendment and binding effect.** SL § 11(a) requires a writing signed by both Parties; the Manager is a signatory only for § 8 — any amendment of § 8 should also require the Manager’s signature.")
B("**Fund counsel identity.** The SL letterhead reads “Graystone Kirkland LLP”; the LPA, the LPA Organizational Expense provision and the IC Memo identify fund counsel as “Graystone Hargrove LLP” (the LPA notice email domain is “graystonekirkland.com”). Confirm the correct entity and that the SL is the GP’s authorised form.")
B("**Signatory title.** Marcus Ridgeline signs the SL as “Managing Partner” of the GP; the LPA signature block and § 13.3(b) describe him as “Managing Member” of the GP (an LLC). Conform the title and obtain evidence of authority.")

def add_runs(p, text, bold=False, italic=False, size=None):
    # **bold** markup support

        r = p.add_run(part); r.bold = bold or (i % 2 == 1); r.italic = italic
