# ---------------- I. Executive summary ----------------
H("I. Executive Summary")
P("We compared each provision of the PBPEPS Side Letter (the “Side Letter” or “SL”) against the corresponding provisions of the RGEF IV LPA (the “LPA”), and tested each statement in the CIO’s email memorandum requesting Investment Committee approval (the “IC Memo”) against both documents. Our bottom line: **the Side Letter delivers several real economic and reporting improvements, but the IC Memo materially overstates what PBPEPS is getting.** Five of the twelve concessions listed in the IC Memo are either misdescribed or are at serious risk of being unenforceable under the LPA’s own conflict rules. The Investment Committee should not rely on the IC Memo as currently written.")
P("Key findings (in order of significance):", bold=True)
B("**The LPA’s “notwithstanding” rule undermines four headline concessions.** LPA § 13.5(b) provides that a Side Letter controls over a conflicting LPA term **only if the Side Letter contains express “notwithstanding” language specifically overriding identified LPA provisions**; otherwise the LPA governs and the side letter is read as supplemental and “not in derogation of” the LPA. The Clawback Enhancement (SL § 7: “In addition to … Section 5.3”), Key Person automatic suspension (SL § 6: “In addition to … Section 6.3”), Guaranteed LPAC Seat (SL § 5(a): “In addition to … Section 8.1”) and Withdrawal Right (SL § 9: no override language at all) each directly contradict an LPA provision but lack the required override. The SL’s own general conflict clause (“the terms of this Side Letter shall control”) does not satisfy § 13.5(b), which demands provision-specific language. The IC Memo’s statement that the SL’s “provisions control in the event of any inconsistency with the LPA” (IC Memo § 5) is therefore incorrect as a matter of the LPA’s terms.")
B("**The IC Memo misstates two hard numbers.** The co-investment threshold is **$125,000,000** in SL § 3(a)–(b), not $100,000,000 as stated in IC Memo Table row 2 and § 4. The withdrawal Deployment Threshold is **50% ($1.39 billion)** in SL § 9, not 40% as stated in IC Memo Table row 11. Both errors make the concessions look more valuable than they are.")
B("**The clawback is described as “notwithstanding the LPA” when it is not**, and its value is overstated. The IC Memo (Table row 10; § 4) says the gross clawback applies “notwithstanding the LPA” — the SL actually says “in addition to.” The IC Memo’s $10 million illustration also implies PBPEPS recovers the full $4.5 million incremental amount; PBPEPS’s economic share of a Fund-level clawback is its ~6.295% Commitment Percentage (≈ $283,000 on those facts). The gross-up is also unsupported by the LPA’s escrow (30% of carry, § 5.3(e)) and personal guaranties (capped at the net-of-tax amount, § 5.3(c)).")
B("**The MFN may be a step backwards, not forward.** SL § 2 (which does override LPA § 10.2) limits PBPEPS’s election to terms granted to LPs whose commitments are **equal to or less than $175 million**. LPA § 10.2 contains no such size limit — an MFN Eligible LP may elect terms from any other LP’s side letter. Read literally, the SL replaces the broader LPA MFN with a narrower one that excludes the largest (and typically best-treated) investors. The IC Memo’s claim that the MFN “ensures PBPEPS receives best available terms” is inaccurate. The SL does improve timing (15-day notice / 90-day election vs. 30/60), retroactivity, and includes co-investment rights (excluded by LPA § 10.2(d)(iii)).")
B("**The Key Person “enhancement” does not change the trigger**, which remains identical to the LPA (Marcus Ridgeline **and** two of three Senior Managing Directors — i.e., three of four Key Persons must depart). Further, a fund-wide suspension of the Investment Period cannot be effected by one LP’s side letter without affecting other LPs (LPA §§ 13.5(c), 14.1(d)), and the SL’s resumption mechanics are in some respects **weaker** than the LPA (resumption on designation of replacements acceptable to PBPEPS alone, bypassing LPAC approval under § 6.3(d), or on a 60% LP vote versus the 75% reinstatement vote in § 6.3(e)).")
B("**The Withdrawal Right conflicts with the LPA’s core closed-end architecture** (§ 3.1(b) irrevocable commitments; § 11.2(b) “no right of redemption or withdrawal” except per §§ 11.2 and 9.1) and would require a cash distribution of NAV out of a pooled vehicle, affecting other LPs. Its enforceability is doubtful; even if enforceable, the Election Period (June 15 – August 14, 2025) has now passed and its status must be confirmed.")
B("**The negligence exculpation standard (SL § 8) is properly overridden but practically limited**: it does not override the LPA § 12.3(a) cap limiting GP liability to its $55.6 million Capital Commitment; SL § 8(b) restricts Fund (not GP) indemnification, which impacts pooled Fund assets and so other LPs (§ 14.1(d)); and the IC Memo omits SL § 8(b) entirely.")
B("**Several drafting errors** require correction: wrong cross-references (SL § 7 to LPA § 5.3(c) for escrow — escrow is § 5.3(e); SL § 9(b) to § 7.2 for valuation — valuation is § 7.3; SL § 11(e) to § 13.4 for notices — notices are § 13.3); a waiver of a non-existent “minimum transfer size requirement” in § 9.1; notices to “addresses set forth in the preamble” where the GP’s address does not appear; outdated CPRA citation (Gov. Code § 6250 et seq. was recodified at § 7920.000 et seq. effective January 1, 2023); and inconsistent fund-counsel name (letterhead “Graystone Kirkland LLP” vs. LPA “Graystone Hargrove LLP”).")
P("Recommendation: The Investment Committee should (i) be provided with a corrected IC Memo; and (ii) PBPEPS should require, before execution (or, if already executed, by way of a confirmatory amendment under SL § 11(a)), an amended Side Letter that adds express provision-specific “notwithstanding” language to SL §§ 5(a), 6, 7 and 9, removes the size limitation from the MFN (or expressly preserves the LPA § 10.2 MFN in addition), corrects the cross-references, and conforms the economic figures. Detailed recommendations appear in Part VIII.", bold=False)

# ---------------- V. Detailed analysis ----------------
H("V. Detailed Analysis of Material Deviations")

H("1. Management Fee (SL § 1; LPA § 4.1)", 2)
P("SL § 1 validly overrides § 4.1 (express “notwithstanding” language, reinforced by § 4.1(g)). The reduction is 25 bps in each period. Our recalculation:")
T(["Period", "LPA Fee", "SL Fee", "Annual Saving", "Period Saving", "Comment"], [
 ["Investment Period (6/15/2022–6/14/2027)", "$3,062,500/yr (1.75% × $175M)", "$2,625,000/yr (1.50% × $175M)", "$437,500", "$2,187,500", "Firm — based on Commitment"],
 ["Post-IP (6/15/2027–6/14/2032)", "1.50% × Invested Capital", "1.25% × Invested Capital", "≤ $437,500", "≤ $2,187,500", "Ceiling only: assumes $175M invested and never reduced by realizations/write-downs; actual likely materially lower"],
 ["Extensions (to 6/14/2034, § 11.1(b))", "1.50% × Invested Capital", "1.25% × Invested Capital", "Variable", "Variable", "Not addressed in IC Memo"],
], widths=[1.4, 1.1, 1.1, 0.8, 0.8, 1.5])
P("Observations: (a) the IC Memo’s “$4,375,000” should be presented as a maximum; a realistic post-IP figure is substantially below $2.19 million because invested capital is reduced by full realizations and write-downs to zero under § 4.1(b); (b) because PBPEPS is MFN-eligible under LPA § 10.2 (and other ≥$150M LPs may elect PBPEPS’s fee term, which is not within any § 10.2(d) carve-out), the GP may later resist granting further concessions; (c) the SL refers to the fee as payable to “the General Partner (or … the Manager)” — § 4.1(c) makes it payable to the Manager; harmless but should be conformed.")

H("2. Most Favored Nation (SL § 2; LPA § 10.2)", 2)
P("SL § 2 is introduced by “Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Section 10.2,” which under § 13.5(b) is effective. That cuts both ways: it means the SL formulation **replaces** § 10.2 for PBPEPS to the extent inconsistent. The key deviations are:")
B("**Narrower universe of source side letters.** SL § 2 extends only to terms granted to LPs “whose Capital Commitment … is equal to or less than” $175 million. LPA § 10.2(b)–(c) has no such limit. PBPEPS (6.295% of commitments) is unlikely to be the largest LP in a $2.78 billion fund; anchor investors with larger commitments typically receive the most favorable terms, and PBPEPS would be excluded from them. This is the single most significant economic drafting point in the SL and is not disclosed in the IC Memo.")
B("**Improvements:** 15-day notice (by October 15, 2022) versus 30 days (October 30, 2022); 90-day versus 60-day election period; redacted copies of side letters rather than a summary; effectiveness from admission (retroactive) versus the LPA’s prospective effect (§ 10.2(c)); a narrower regulatory carve-out (only terms “not applicable to the Investor”) versus § 10.2(d)(i)’s broad carve-out for any public-pension accommodation; and co-investment rights are included (§ 10.2(d)(iii) excludes them). The SL is silent on the LPAC exclusion (§ 10.2(d)(iv)).")
B("**Gaps:** limited to “economic or reporting” terms (governance protections such as key person, transfer, excuse and LPAC rights may fall outside); no express coverage of side letters entered into after the Final Close (e.g., with transferees) or of supplemental MFN Notices under § 10.2(e); no remedy beyond self-executing effectiveness if the GP fails to give notice.")
P("Recommendation: delete the size limitation or, at a minimum, add: “The rights of the Investor under this Section 2 are in addition to, and not in limitation of, the rights of the Investor as an MFN Eligible LP under Section 10.2 of the Partnership Agreement, and the Investor may elect under whichever provision is more favorable.”")

H("3. Co-Investment Rights (SL § 3)", 2)
P("The IC Memo states the threshold twice as $100 million; SL § 3(a), § 3(b) and the closing paragraph of § 3 all state **$125,000,000**. The SL’s worked example (Fund equity $200M; excess $75M; allocation $4,717,500 at 6.29%) is arithmetically correct at the rounded rate (≈$4,721,000 at Schedule A’s 6.2950%). Given the Fund’s $100–$750 million EV focus and the 20% single-company limit (≈$556 million, § 6.2(a)), equity cheques above $125 million will occur only in the larger transactions, so the right will be exercised infrequently. Other points: (a) the definition of the Fund’s “aggregate equity commitment (including any equity commitment made through a co-investment vehicle)” is circular and could inflate or deflate the threshold; (b) the obligation is “subject to [the GP’s] fiduciary obligations” and regulatory constraints — a broad escape; (c) co-investment vehicles organised by the GP are “Affiliates” under the LPA definition, so § 8.2(a)(i) LPAC conflict consent may be required; (d) expenses of the co-investment vehicle and broken-deal cost sharing are unaddressed; (e) the SL right is protected from other LPs’ MFN by § 10.2(d)(iii), which is favorable to PBPEPS’s exclusivity.")

H("4. Transfer Rights (SL § 4; LPA § 9.1)", 2)
P("SL § 4 effectively removes the GP’s § 9.1(a) sole-discretion consent for transfers to US state governmental pension plans, subject to notice, assumption, legal opinion and compliance conditions. Points of deviation and risk:")
B("**Competitor bar.** LPA § 9.1(b) opens with “Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement” and prohibits transfers to any Competitor. The “Competitor” definition (§ 1.1) expressly sweeps in “pension system[s]” that manage or advise a fund with a substantially similar strategy. A GP could argue that a state pension plan with an in-house growth equity or co-investment program is a Competitor, and that SL § 4’s general override of “Section 9.1” does not reach § 9.1(b)(iii). The SL should state expressly that a governmental pension plan shall not be deemed a Competitor solely by reason of its in-house investment activities.")
B("**Eligibility bars retained by implication.** The SL does not expressly preserve or waive the § 9.1(b)(i)–(ii) qualified purchaser / accredited investor requirements; the legal opinion requirement partly covers this. Clarity is recommended.")
B("**Non-existent requirement.** SL § 4 waives “the minimum transfer size requirements set forth in Section 9.1” — § 9.1 contains no minimum transfer size. Either a requirement was dropped from the LPA or the SL was drafted from a different precedent; confirm.")
B("**Costs.** SL waives any “transfer fee or administrative charge”; § 9.1(e) separately requires the transferor to bear the Fund’s legal, accounting and administrative costs. The SL’s waiver is broader in wording only as to “fee or charge” — clarify that § 9.1(e) costs are also waived (or capped).")
B("**IC Memo overstatement.** The IC Memo’s reference to “co-investing sister funds” is not supported; only governmental pension plans organised under US state law qualify. Non-governmental affiliates must use § 9.1(f), which requires PBPEPS to remain jointly and severally liable.")
B("**Positive:** transferees inherit SL rights (§ 4 and § 11(b)), including the negligence standard (SL § 8(a)), and PBPEPS is not made jointly and severally liable post-transfer (contrast § 9.1(f)(iv)).")

H("5. LPAC Seat (SL § 5(a); LPA § 8.1)", 2)
P("LPA § 8.1(c) states that “No Limited Partner shall have the right to demand appointment to the LPAC … This Agreement does not provide for any automatic appointment, guaranteed seat, or other mandatory LPAC membership right for any Limited Partner,” and § 8.1(b) permits the GP to “remove and replace LPAC members at any time in its sole discretion.” SL § 5(a) is expressed to be “In addition to the provisions of Section 8.1” and expressly acknowledges that the LPAC operates “in accordance with Section 8.1.” Under § 13.5(b), absent a “notwithstanding” override, the LPA governs and the SL is “not in derogation of” it. Although the SL calls the seat a “binding obligation” and “material inducement,” the GP has a credible argument that it may remove PBPEPS under § 8.1(b). PBPEPS would at most have a contract claim against the GP (not a right to sit). Additional points: the seat would be lost under § 8.1(b) if PBPEPS’s commitment is reduced below $100 million (e.g., through excuse reductions under SL § 5(b)/LPA § 9.2(d) or partial transfers); and the seat is personal to PBPEPS (it is not MFN-able by others under § 10.2(d)(iv)).")
P("Fix: “Notwithstanding Sections 8.1(a), 8.1(b) and 8.1(c) of the Partnership Agreement, the Investor shall be entitled to appoint one member of the LPAC for the term of the Fund, and the General Partner shall not remove the Investor’s representative without the Investor’s consent, provided the Investor’s Capital Commitment is not less than $100,000,000 (disregarding reductions resulting from excused investments).”")

H("6. Excuse Rights (SL § 5(b); LPA § 9.2)", 2)
P("SL § 5(b) validly overrides § 9.2 (express “notwithstanding”) and is a genuine expansion: § 9.2(a) and (f) expressly prohibit excuse based on “board-adopted investment parameters, social responsibility policies [or] environmental policies,” whereas SL § 5(b)(ii) allows excuse on an objective 15% revenue test irrespective of statutory compulsion. Issues: (a) **Timing** — the 15-business-day notice period runs from receipt of the capital call notice, and § 3.2(a)(iv) permits a funding date only 15 business days after notice; PBPEPS should require advance notice of prospective investments (not merely the call) and confirm that a timely excuse notice suspends the funding obligation; (b) **Determination** — because SL § 5(b) is stated to be “in addition to” § 9.2, the GP could argue the § 9.2(c) GP good-faith determination applies; the SL should make PBPEPS’s determination conclusive for § 5(b)(ii); (c) **Statutory basis** — the IC Memo characterises California Government Code §§ 7500–7914 as imposing “divestment mandates related to tobacco, firearms, and thermal coal.” Several California divestment statutes apply by their terms only to specified systems (e.g., CalPERS/CalSTRS); PBPEPS’s regulatory counsel should confirm which mandates actually bind PBPEPS. To the extent they do not, SL § 5(b)(ii) (the revenue test) remains the operative protection; (d) **Overlap** — LPA § 6.2(c)(ii) already prohibits natural resources, mining or extractive investments, so thermal coal producers are largely excluded at Fund level; (e) the forfeiture language (“share of any distributions attributable to such excused investment shall be forfeited”) is consistent with § 9.2(e) but should be clarified to confirm no penalty on PBPEPS’s other investments and that Management Fees are not charged on the reduced commitment.")

H("7. Key Person (SL § 6; LPA § 6.3)", 2)
P("The IC Memo presents automatic suspension as “materially stronger protection.” Our analysis is that the protection is largely illusory as drafted:")
B("**No override.** SL § 6 is “In addition to” § 6.3. LPA § 6.3(c) states the Investment Period “shall be suspended **only** upon the affirmative vote or written consent of Limited Partners holding at least sixty percent (60%)” — a direct conflict. Under § 13.5(b), the LPA governs.")
B("**Fund-wide effect.** The Investment Period is a single fund-wide period. An automatic suspension for all LPs triggered by one LP’s side letter would “directly or indirectly alter” other LPs’ rights (§ 14.1(d); § 13.5(c)). A PBPEPS-only suspension (i.e., excuse from new-investment capital calls during a KPE) is the enforceable alternative and should be drafted as such.")
B("**Trigger unchanged.** Both documents require that Marcus Ridgeline **and** at least two of three SMDs cease to devote ≥75% of their time (§ 6.3(b)). Three of four Key Persons must depart before anything happens. A market-standard investor ask would be “Marcus Ridgeline **or** any two SMDs.” The final sentence of § 6.3(b) is also internally garbled and should be clarified.")
B("**Weaker resumption.** SL § 6 resumes the Investment Period on the earlier of (a) replacements “reasonably acceptable to the Investor” or (b) a 60% LP vote. LPA § 6.3(d) requires LPAC majority approval of replacements with comparable qualifications, and § 6.3(e) requires a 75% vote to reinstate after an uncured KPE. If SL § 6 were effective, it would allow resumption on a lower threshold than the LPA.")
B("**Follow-on cap.** SL § 6 caps follow-ons during suspension at 15% of Commitments (consistent with § 6.1(b)); LPA § 6.3(c) contains no cap during suspension — a modest improvement.")

H("8. Clawback Enhancement (SL § 7; LPA § 5.3)", 2)
P("LPA § 5.3(b) provides that the Clawback Amount “shall be calculated net of taxes … at an assumed combined federal and state tax rate of forty-five percent (45%)” and that the “maximum Clawback Amount” is the excess reduced by 45%. SL § 7 is “In addition to” § 5.3 and directly contradicts § 5.3(b). Under § 13.5(b), the LPA formula governs. The IC Memo states the enhancement applies “notwithstanding the LPA” (Table row 10; § 4) — that is not what the SL says.")
P("Even if enforceable, the economics are overstated. The clawback is paid “to the Fund, for distribution to the Limited Partners” (§ 5.3(a)), so PBPEPS’s benefit is its pro rata share. On the IC Memo’s own illustration ($10M excess carry): LPA net clawback = $5.5M; gross = $10M; incremental Fund-level recovery = $4.5M; PBPEPS share ≈ 6.295% × $4.5M ≈ **$283,000**, not $4.5M. SL § 7’s phrasing that “the full amount of any excess carried interest distributions … shall be returned to the Investor” is ambiguous and should be clarified to refer to the Investor’s attributable share.")
P("Security mismatch: § 5.3(e) escrow is only 30% of cumulative carry and the § 5.3(c) personal guaranties cover only the net-of-tax amount. SL § 7 refers to the escrow as “Section 5.3(c)” (wrong; it is § 5.3(e)) and requires the GP to “ensure” escrow sufficiency without specifying a top-up mechanism. The SL should expressly override §§ 5.3(b) and 5.3(c), require guaranties of the gross amount, and specify a PBPEPS-specific escrow reserve or top-up.")

H("9. Exculpation and Indemnification (SL § 8; LPA Article XII)", 2)
P("SL § 8 properly overrides §§ 12.1 and 12.2 and is contemplated by § 12.2(d). However: (a) **§ 12.3(a) cap** — GP aggregate liability to the Fund and LPs is capped at the GP’s $55.6M Capital Commitment (clawback excepted) and SL § 8 does not override § 12.3; (b) **scope** — SL § 8(c) defines “investment decisions in which the Investor’s capital is deployed” to cover virtually every Fund investment, which is favorable but heightens the GP’s argument that the provision affects the Fund as a whole; (c) **Fund indemnity** — SL § 8(b) limits the Fund’s duty to indemnify the GP/Manager for negligence; because indemnity is paid from pooled Fund assets, this indirectly benefits all LPs, but if the GP contends it alters the indemnification relationship with other LPs (§ 14.1(d)) enforceability may be contested; (d) **Manager** — the Manager signs only an acknowledgement “solely with respect to Section 8”; the Investment Management Agreement (not reviewed) should be checked for inconsistent exculpation; (e) **forum** — claims proceed by AAA arbitration in Wilmington (§ 13.2), with each side bearing its own costs (§ 13.2(d)); (f) the IC Memo omits the § 8(b) indemnity change altogether.")

H("10. Withdrawal Right (SL § 9; LPA §§ 3.1(b), 11.2(b))", 2)
P("The IC Memo states the Deployment Threshold as 40%; SL § 9 states **50%** ($1,390,000,000 of $2,780,000,000), measured on “funded investments and binding commitments” as of June 15, 2025. LPA § 3.1(b) makes commitments irrevocable “except as expressly provided in this Agreement,” and § 11.2(b) states that no LP may withdraw “except as set forth in this Section 11.2 and Section 9.1” and that the Fund has “no right of redemption or withdrawal.” SL § 9 contains no override language and therefore, under § 13.5(b), is at material risk of being unenforceable. In addition, payment of PBPEPS’s share of NAV in cash within 180 days would require liquidation or borrowing at Fund level, diluting or burdening other LPs (§§ 13.5(c), 14.1(d)) — notwithstanding SL § 9’s statement that other LPs need not increase commitments.")
P("Mechanical issues: (a) the valuation cross-reference to “Section 7.2” is to the Fiscal Year provision — valuation is § 7.3; (b) the sequence of a 60-day Election Period followed by a 90-day Withdrawal Notice and a 180-day valuation/payment window leaves PBPEPS exposed to capital calls during the notice period (SL § 9(d) only preserves calls “issued prior to the date of the Withdrawal Notice,” which is favorable, but the “effective date” of withdrawal is not defined); (c) “binding commitments” counting toward deployment is GP-favorable and undefined; (d) the GP’s reserve right for contingent liabilities is uncapped; (e) **timing** — the Election Period ran from June 15 to August 14, 2025. If the SL was executed, PBPEPS should confirm whether the Deployment Threshold was tested and whether the right lapsed.")

H("11. Reporting and CPRA (SL § 10; LPA §§ 7.1, 10.1)", 2)
P("SL § 10(a) properly overrides § 7.1 and shortens deadlines (60/90 days) and adds monthly portfolio summaries. However, the closing paragraph converts these into “commercially reasonable efforts” obligations with a no-breach carve-out for circumstances beyond the GP’s control; the IC Memo does not mention this. The 90-day audited deadline may be impracticable if the auditor’s timetable is driven by the LPA’s 120-day standard; PBPEPS should confirm with the GP that Haverford Accounting Group has been engaged on that basis.")
P("SL § 10(b) properly overrides § 10.1 as to GP designation practice, but it does not expressly amend PBPEPS’s own confidentiality covenant in § 10.1(a), whose exceptions (§ 10.1(b)) do not mention public records laws. SL § 11(f)(ii) covers disclosure of the SL itself “as may be required by applicable law … including … the CPRA,” but not Fund information generally. Recommended: add an express carve-out permitting PBPEPS to make any disclosure it reasonably determines is required under the CPRA (now Gov. Code § 7920.000 et seq.) or other public records law, including disclosures mandated for alternative investment vehicles. Also: the ≥10-business-day prior notice to the GP “where practicable” can conflict with the CPRA’s 10-day initial response period; the “designated as confidential by such portfolio company” exception lets portfolio companies self-designate; and the statutory citation (§ 6250 et seq.) should be updated.")

H("12. General Provisions (SL § 11)", 2)
B("**No governing law or dispute resolution clause.** The IC Memo’s LPA baseline cites Delaware law (§ 13.1) and AAA arbitration (§ 13.2), but the SL itself is silent. Because the SL “forms a part of” the LPA, LPA §§ 13.1–13.2 likely apply; this should be stated expressly. PBPEPS should also confirm whether, as a California public entity, it requires a California-venue or sovereign-immunity reservation.")
B("**Notices.** SL § 11(e) refers to “Section 13.4” for notice mechanics (§ 13.4 is Successors and Assigns; notices are § 13.3) and to addresses “set forth in the preamble,” which include only PBPEPS’s address.")
B("**Amendment and binding effect.** SL § 11(a) requires a writing signed by both Parties; the Manager is a signatory only for § 8 — any amendment of § 8 should also require the Manager’s signature.")
B("**Fund counsel identity.** The SL letterhead reads “Graystone Kirkland LLP”; the LPA, the LPA Organizational Expense provision and the IC Memo identify fund counsel as “Graystone Hargrove LLP” (the LPA notice email domain is “graystonekirkland.com”). Confirm the correct entity and that the SL is the GP’s authorised form.")
B("**Signatory title.** Marcus Ridgeline signs the SL as “Managing Partner” of the GP; the LPA signature block and § 13.3(b) describe him as “Managing Member” of the GP (an LLC). Conform the title and obtain evidence of authority.")

I wrote the deviation analysis memo comparing the PBPEPS side letter to the RGEF IV LPA and checking the CIO's IC approval memo. Its main finding is that the IC memo overstates what PBPEPS gets: it misstates the co-investment threshold ($125M in the side letter, not $100M) and the withdrawal threshold (50%, not 40%), and it overstates the clawback and MFN terms. Four other terms are probably unenforceable because LPA §13.5(b) requires express "notwithstanding" override language, which the side-letter sections for the clawback, key person, LPAC seat and withdrawal right lack.
